chunks: Suleiman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayoob al-Lakhmy told me, saying: Abdul Wahhab ibn Kharajat narrated to us, saying: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ja'far al-Abasi narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn al-Hussein al-Alavi narrated to us, from his father Al-Hussein ibn Zayd, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), saying:

Three [characteristics]: whoever does not possess them is not from me nor from Allah, the Exalted. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what are they? He said: Forbearance by which he repels the ignorance of the ignorant; good character by which he lives among the people; and piety (war') which restrains him from the sins of Allah, the Exalted.

key_terms.حُسْنُ خُلُقٍ: Good character or excellent manners in social interactions
key_terms.حِلْمٌ: Forbearance or patience in the face of ignorance or provocation
key_terms.وَرَعٌ: Piety or God-consciousness that restrains one from sins

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics that define a true follower of the Prophet according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a definitive criterion for spiritual lineage, linking the Prophet’s character directly to divine attributes. The triad of *hilm* (forbearance), *husn al-khuluq* (good character), and *wara'* (piety/conscientiousness) serves as the ethical foundation for Shia moral theology, emphasizing that true faith is manifested through social conduct and restraint from minor sins. This narration underscores the Shia belief in the inseparability of theological identity and practical ethics.
